preRegistration.title: Pre-registration — PACD (Public Assistance and Complaints Desk)
preRegistration.detail: Ask for information and get the form to fill up. Staff check whether you have an appointment.
branches: With an appointment — you are sent directly to the specified clinic.
Without an appointment — you are given a number to start triage.

steps.title: Triage Nurse
steps.detail: Present your queue number and answer the nurse's initial screening questions.

steps.title: Vital Signs
steps.detail: Staff record your basic vital signs before screening.

steps.title: Screening / Verification
steps.requirementNote: Have your PhilHealth Member Data Record (MDR) ready, if available
steps.detail: Staff check for an existing record, follow-up status, and PhilHealth.
branches: With PhilHealth — proceed to the PCU for member verification.
Without PhilHealth — you are directed to the Social Worker for registration.

steps.title: Registration
steps.requirementNote: Government-issued ID; for infants or children, a photocopy of the birth certificate
steps.detail: New patients are registered; existing patients have their records pulled.

steps.title: Cashier
steps.requirementNote: Present a qualifying ID at the cashier if you are eligible for the ₱0 rate
steps.detail: Newly registered patients with no existing record pay ₱150. Senior citizens, PWDs, and other eligible patients pay ₱0 upon presentation of a qualifying ID.

steps.title: Clinic
steps.detail: You are directed to your intended clinic.

steps.title: Queue Number
steps.detail: On arrival, get a queueing number from the guard.

steps.title: Vital Signs
steps.detail: Wait at the VS area for the initial assessment.

steps.title: PhilHealth Verification
steps.requirementNote: Have your PhilHealth Member Data Record (MDR) ready, if available
steps.detail: Proceed to PhilHealth verification.

steps.title: Registration
steps.detail: After verification, proceed to patient registration.

steps.title: Nurse Triage
steps.detail: The triage nurse evaluates your condition and determines the appropriate consultation process.

steps.title: Wait for Consultation
steps.detail: Monitor the queueing screen for your queue number to be called.

steps.title: Doctor's Consultation
steps.detail: Once called, proceed to the designated OPD consultation cubicle.

steps.title: Post-Consultation Instructions
steps.detail: You are told where to go next based on the doctor's orders.
destinations: Other required diagnostic or treatment services

steps.title: Follow-Up
steps.detail: If a follow-up consultation is required, first complete the requested laboratory tests, X-rays, or other examinations, then return for follow-up per staff instructions.

radiology.introText: This is general guidance. Your doctor's request has the exact instructions for your study.
radiology.contactPrefix: If you are unsure, call Radiology at
generalItems: Bring your doctor's request form and a valid ID.
Bring previous films, CDs or reports of earlier imaging, if you have them, so they can be compared.
Arrive early so there is time to register before your study.
Wear loose, comfortable clothing. You may be asked to change into a hospital gown.
Remove metal objects, jewellery and hairpins before the study.
safetyNotices: Tell the staff before your study if you are pregnant or might be pregnant.
Before an MRI, tell the staff if you have a pacemaker, an implant, surgical clips or any metal in your body.
If your study uses contrast, tell the staff if you have a contrast allergy, kidney disease, or take medicine for diabetes.

guides.title: X-ray and fluoroscopy
items: Most plain X-rays need no special preparation.
Some fluoroscopy studies need preparation before the day. Follow the instructions on your doctor's request.

guides.title: Ultrasound
items: Some ultrasound studies need preparation, such as not eating beforehand or coming with a full bladder.
Which preparation applies depends on the body part being scanned. Check your doctor's request or ask Radiology.

guides.title: CT scan
items: Some CT scans use contrast. Your doctor's request or Radiology will tell you if yours does and how to prepare.
Tell the staff about allergies, kidney disease and diabetes medicine before a contrast study.

guides.title: MRI
items: Tell the staff about pacemakers, implants, surgical clips or metal fragments before you enter the scanner room.
Remove all metal objects. Tell the staff if you are uncomfortable in enclosed spaces.

guides.title: Mammography
items: Tell the staff if you are pregnant, might be pregnant, or are breastfeeding.
Bring previous mammograms if you have them, so they can be compared.
